newsitem.title: UK: British Midland to start Brussels lobster service.
newsitem.headline: British Midland to start Brussels lobster service.

text.p: British Midland is planning to launch a London Heathrow to Brussels refrigerated trucking service this August to carry live lobsters flown in from Canada, said cargo manager Terry Greetham.
"People in Continental Europe are eating more and more lobsters, of which there are many more available than in the past. It is very much a growth business," he said.
"There appears to be an insatiable demand for this product on the Continent and despite the high cost involved in flying the lobsters live, customers are prepared to pay the price," he said.
He added that the trucks would augment the Boeing 737 bellyhold capacity the carrier already uses to carry seafood to Belgium and France.
The lobsters are flown from Halifax, Nova Scotia, by Air Canada.
Greetham said British Midland was also seeing growth in the transportation of live eels bred by the Toonbridge Lough Nealgh fishery co-operative in Ireland and destined for Amsterdam.
